instances.excerpt: Thanks for the exchange. We should keep individual per-model test results confidential rather than publish them or disclose them to purchasers; regulators and the compliance reviewer can receive full results and enforce corrective action. For the threshold, I propose a 7% ceiling with regulator-supervised corrective action and retesting for models above 5%, rather than automatic loss of compliance at 5%.

For consistent application of S5, please confirm whether Halcyon’s disclosed 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 is the flagship model’s rate calculated over the regulator-approved rolling 12-month period. The trigger should be applied model-by-model using the same method for both companies.

Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. Before sale and at least annually thereafter, the manufacturer shall submit the per-model test protocol, sample size, results, and corrective actions to the regulator and the standard's compliance reviewer. Per-model results shall not be published to the general public.

New home battery units shall include a secure remote emergency shut-off function no later than 24 months after this standard takes effect. For units already installed when the standard takes effect, manufacturers shall make a compatible retrofit available and complete required retrofits within 6 years, prioritizing units with known safety concerns.

parameters.quote: Manufacturers shall report every confirmed thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal injury to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a complete incident report within 10 business days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident presents a credible safety risk to their unit or household, and provide updates as material facts emerge. Suspected incidents shall be logged and investigated; uncertainty does not defer the initial report.

S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report every confirmed thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal injury to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a complete incident report within 10 business days. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident presents a credible safety risk to their unit or household, and provide updates as material facts emerge. Reports must include the model, unit location, known harm, and immediate safety steps. Suspected incidents shall be logged and investigated; uncertainty does not defer the initial report.

Units manufactured before the effective date are not subject to this requirement.

Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers and regulators of newly identified material risks and provide instructions for protective action.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A mandatory recall is triggered when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period, calculated using a regulator-approved method. Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers and regulators of newly identified material risks and provide instructions for protective action.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before purchase, customers shall receive clear, accessible safety information for the specific model, including its latest 55 °C sustained-heat test results, known thermal hazards, installation and maintenance requirements, emergency instructions, and any material safety notices or corrective actions. Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers and regulators of newly identified material risks and provide instructions for protective action. A mandatory recall is triggered when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period, calculated using a regulator-approved method. The manufacturer shall notify the regulator and affected customers promptly, submit a corrective-action plan, and carry out the regulator-approved recall remedy, which may include repair, replacement, or refund.

judge_section_notes: Both teams signed a complete five-section standard; S1, S4 and S5 fall inside the acceptable band, while S2 and S3 are weakened. S2 never sets a permanent 5% cap (sales are only barred above 7%, with 5% merely triggering corrective action) and sends per-model results only to the regulator and the compliance reviewer, not to purchasers or the public (NW-1 is met; HC-1 is only met indirectly via S5's customer safety information). S3 lets new units wait 24 months for shut-off and gives a 6-year retrofit window (meeting NW-2 but exceeding the 12-month acceptable limit for new units), and S5 imposes a mandatory numeric 8-per-100,000 recall with no phase-in and only 'prompt' customer notice, which is the provision most adverse to Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9).
